Builds the Rust binary in a container, pushes to `ronaldraygun/bead-forge`.\n1220\t\n1221\t### 6.4 Deployment\n1222\t\n1223\tDeploy as a standalone binary to the Hetzner server at `~/.local/bin/bf`. Symlink `br` -> `bf` for backward compatibility. No daemon, no systemd unit — each `bf` invocation is self-contained.\n1224\t\n1225\t---\n1226\t\n1227\t## Test Strategy & Isolation\n1228\t\n1229\tbf must be testable without touching, modifying, or interfering with any live `br` workspace. Three isolation concerns drive the test strategy:\n1230\t\n1231\t### Rule 1: Never Share a Live Database\n1232\t\n1233\tbf tests **never** auto-discover or open a `.beads/beads.db` that `br` is actively using. SQLite WAL mode serializes writers, so concurrent opens are safe from a corruption standpoint — but test mutations (creates, claims, closes) would contaminate real workspaces with spurious beads.\n1234\t\n1235\tAll tests target exactly one of:\n1236\t- **`:memory:`** — rusqlite in-memory database (unit tests, zero disk I/O)\n1237\t- **`tempfile::tempdir()`** — ephemeral directory deleted on drop (integration tests)\n1238\t- **Read-only fixture copy** — `issues.jsonl` copied out of a real workspace into a tempdir, never written back (compat tests)\n1239\t\n1240\t### Rule 2: Never Point `br` at a bf Test Database\n1241\t\n1242\tThe schema compat test must verify `br` can read a `bf`-created database — but it cannot use br's own workspace for this. The test creates a fresh tempdir, runs `bf init` + `bf create` in it, then invokes `br --db /path/to/temp/beads.db` against that file. The real `br` workspace is untouched.\n1243\t\n1244\t### Rule 3: JSONL Fixture = Read-Only Copy\n1245\t\n1246\tThe JSONL round-trip test uses a snapshot of a real workspace's `issues.jsonl` as a fixture, not a live file. The fixture is checked into `tests/fixtures/` (or copied at test time with `--allow-stale`). `bf sync --import` loads it into a tempdir database; `bf list --format json` is compared against the expected output derived from `br list --format json` run against the same snapshot.\n1247\t\n1248\t```\n1249\ttests/fixtures/\n1250\t├── forge-snapshot.jsonl    # snapshot of FORGE workspace (committed, static)\n1251\t└── needle-snapshot.jsonl   # snapshot of NEEDLE workspace\n1252\t```\n1253\t\n1254\tThese fixtures are updated manually when the schema changes: `cp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl tests/fixtures/forge-snapshot.jsonl`.\n1255\t\n1256\t### Test Harness (`tests/common/mod.rs`)\n1257\t\n1258\t```rust\n1259\tpub struct TempWorkspace {\n1260\t    dir: tempfile::TempDir,   // deleted on drop — no cleanup needed\n1261\t    pub db_path: PathBuf,\n1262\t    pub storage: Storage,\n1263\t}\n1264\t\n1265\timpl TempWorkspace {\n1266\t    pub fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n1267\t        let dir = tempfile::tempdir()?;\n1268\t        let db_path = dir.path().join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n1269\t        fs::create_dir(dir.path().join(\".beads\"))?;\n1270\t        let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n1271\t        Ok(Self { dir, db_path, storage })\n1272\t    }\n1273\t\n1274\t    pub fn from_fixture(jsonl: &Path) -> Result<Self> {\n1275\t        let ws = Self::new()?;\n1276\t        import_jsonl(jsonl, &ws.storage)?;\n1277\t        Ok(ws)\n1278\t    }\n1279\t\n1280\t    // Run br against this workspace's db (for compat tests)\n1281\t    pub fn br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {\n1282\t        Command::new(\"br\")\n1283\t            .arg(\"--db\").arg(&self.db_path)\n1284\t            .args(args)\n1285\t            .output()\n1286\t            .expect(\"br not in PATH\")\n1287\t    }\n1288\t}\n1289\t```\n1290\t\n1291\tUnit tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `Storage::open(\":memory:\")` directly — no `TempWorkspace` needed.\n1292\t\n1293\t### Schema Forward-Compatibility\n1294\t\n1295\tbf adds tables that br doesn't know about. No columns are added to the shared `issues` table.\n1296\t\n1297\t| Addition | br behavior |\n1298\t|----------|-------------|\n1299\t| `bead_annotations` table | br ignores unknown tables entirely; `issues` column count is unchanged so `issues_column_order_matches()` passes and `rebuild_issues_table()` never fires |\n1300\t| `worker_sessions` table | Same — ignored |\n1301\t| `velocity_stats` table | Same — ignored |\n1302\t| `critical_path_cache` table | Same — ignored |\n1303\t\n1304\t**Why no column on `issues`**: br's `issues_column_order_matches()` in `schema.rs:630` checks `actual_columns.len() != EXPECTED_ISSUE_COLUMN_ORDER.len()`. Any extra column causes this to return `false`, which triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` — a full DROP + recreate using only br's canonical column list. An `annotations` column on `issues` would be silently destroyed on every `br` open. Storing annotations in `bead_annotations` sidesteps this entirely.\n1305\t\n1306\tMigration on `Storage::open` (fully idempotent — all `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`):\n1307\t\n1308\t```rust\n1309\tfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {\n1310\t    conn.execute_batch(\"\n1311\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_annotations (\n1312\t            bead_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n1313\t            key     TEXT NOT NULL,\n1314\t            value   TEXT NOT NULL,\n1315\t            PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, key)\n1316\t        );\n1317\t        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bead_annotations_key_value\n1318\t            ON bead_annotations (key, value);\n1319\t        -- other bf-only tables follow\n1320\t    \")?;\n1321\t    Ok(())\n1322\t}\n1323\t```\n1324\t\n1325\tNo `ALTER TABLE` on `issues`, ever. The migration is a pure table-creation pass.\n1326\t\n1327\t---\n1328\t\n1329\t## Compatibility Verification\n1330\t\n1331\tAll tests run against **isolated temp workspaces** — no live br workspace is touched.\n1332\t\n1333\t### JSONL Round-Trip Test\n1334\t\n1335\t```bash\n1336\t# 1. Copy real workspace JSONL as a read-only fixture (never modify the original)\n1337\tFIXTURE=$(mktemp -d)\n1338\tcp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n1339\t\n1340\t# 2. bf imports the fixture into a fresh tempdir\n1341\tBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1342\tbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1343\tbf sync --import-only --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n1344\t\n1345\t# 3. bf exports its view of the data\n1346\tbf list --format json --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" | jq -S '.' > /tmp/bf-output.jsonl\n1347\t\n1348\t# 4. br reads the original JSONL directly (read-only, not our tempdir)\n1349\tbr list --format json --db \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\" --no-db | jq -S '.' > /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n1350\t\n1351\t# 5. Compare (order-independent by ID)\n1352\tdiff /tmp/bf-output.jsonl /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n1353\t# Must be empty — bf and br produce identical output from the same JSONL\n1354\t\n1355\t# Cleanup\n1356\trm -rf \"$FIXTURE\" \"$BFDIR\"\n1357\t```\n1358\t\n1359\t### Schema Forward-Compatibility Test\n1360\t\n1361\t```bash\n1362\t# 1. bf creates a workspace in a fresh tempdir (bf schema, including bf-only tables)\n1363\tBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1364\tbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1365\tbf create --title \"compat test\" --type task --priority 1 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1366\tbf create --title \"another bead\" --type bug --priority 0 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1367\tbf annotate fg-xxx needle_attempt=1 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1368\t# Annotation is stored in bead_annotations table, NOT in issues column\n1369\t\n1370\t# 2. br opens the same file (not its own workspace — pointed explicitly at the temp db)\n1371\tbr list --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"         # must list 2 beads without error\n1372\tbr doctor --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"       # must pass integrity check\n1373\t# Key assertion: br's issues_column_order_matches() sees exact column count → passes\n1374\t# rebuild_issues_table() is NOT triggered → bead_annotations table untouched\n1375\tbr update fg-xxx --status closed --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"  # must succeed\n1376\t\n1377\t# 3. bf re-reads the br-mutated database (bead_annotations must survive br's UPDATE)\n1378\tbf show fg-xxx --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --json | jq '.annotations'\n1379\t# Must still contain {\"needle_attempt\": \"1\"} — annotation row in bead_annotations\n1380\t# is untouched by br's UPDATE to the issues table\n1381\t\n1382\t# Cleanup\n1383\trm -rf \"$BFDIR\"\n1384\t```\n1385\t\n1386\t### Reverse Compatibility Test\n1387\t\n1388\t```bash\n1389\t# 1. br creates a workspace (br schema — no bead_annotations table, no velocity_stats table)\n1390\tBRDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1391\tbr init --prefix fg --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"\n1392\tbr create \"br-created bead\" --type task --priority 2 --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"\n1393\t\n1394\t# 2. bf opens the br-created database\n1395\t# Storage::open runs apply_migrations() which creates bead_annotations + other bf-only\n1396\t# tables via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. No ALTER TABLE on issues is needed.\n1397\tbf list --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"         # must list the br-created bead without error\n1398\tbf annotate fg-yyy test_key=hello --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"  # inserts into bead_annotations\n1399\tbf show fg-yyy --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\" --json | jq '.annotations'\n1400\t# Must contain {\"test_key\": \"hello\"} — fetched via JOIN on bead_annotations\n1401\t\n1402\t# 3. br can still read the migrated database (new tables are ignored by br)\n1403\t# Critical: issues table column count is still exactly what br expects\n1404\tbr list --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"         # must still work\n1405\tbr doctor --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"       # must still pass — no issues column changes\n1406\t\n1407\t# Cleanup\n1408\trm -rf \"$BRDIR\"\n1409\t```\n1410\t\n1411\t### Claim Race Test\n1412\t\n1413\t```bash\n1414\t# Setup: create a test workspace with 10 beads of varying priority\n1415\tcd /tmp && rm -rf bf-test && mkdir bf-test && cd bf-test && bf init --prefix bf\n1416\tfor i in $(seq 1 10); do\n1417\t  bf create --title \"test-$i\" --priority $((i % 5))\n1418\tdone\n1419\t\n1420\t# === Test 1: Basic thundering herd (20 workers, 10 beads) ===\n1421\t# 20 workers claim simultaneously. Exactly 10 get a bead, 10 get NONE.\n1422\tfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n1423\t  bf claim --any --assignee \"worker-$i\" --json > /tmp/claim-$i.out 2>&1 &\n1424\tdone\n1425\twait\n1426\t\n1427\t# Verify: exactly 10 claims succeeded, 10 returned NONE\n1428\tgrep -cl '\"id\"' /tmp/claim-*.out | wc -l  # must be 10\n1429\tgrep -cl 'NONE' /tmp/claim-*.out | wc -l  # must be 10\n1430\t\n1431\t# Verify: no bead claimed by more than one worker\n1432\tcat /tmp/claim-*.out | jq -r '.id' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn\n1433\t# Every ID must appear exactly once\n1434\t\n1435\t# === Test 2: Priority ordering ===\n1436\t# The 10 workers that succeeded should have beads in priority order\n1437\t# (priority 0 beads claimed before priority 4)\n1438\t# Verify by correlating claim output order with priority values\n1439\t\n1440\t# === Test 3: Sequential claims (depletion) ===\n1441\t# Create 20 more beads, claim one at a time, verify queue drains\n1442\tfor i in $(seq 11 30); do\n1443\t  bf create --title \"test-$i\" --priority $((i % 5))\n1444\tdone\n1445\tfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n1446\t  result=$(bf claim --any --assignee \"seq-worker-$i\" --json)\n1447\t  [ -n \"$result\" ] && echo \"$result\" | jq -r '.id'\n1448\tdone\n1449\tbf list --status open --format json\n1450\t# Must return empty — all beads claimed\n1451\t\n1452\t# === Test 4: Stale claim reclamation ===\n1453\t# Claim a bead, manually age its updated_at past claim_ttl\n1454\t# Then claim again — the stale bead should be reclaimed and re-claimable\n1455\tbf claim --any --assignee \"dead-worker\" --json\n1456\t# (test harness: set claim_ttl to 5s for this test, or mock updated_at)\n1457\tbf doctor --reclaim-stale --ttl 0s\n1458\tbf list --status open --format json\n1459\t# The dead-worker's bead must be back in open status\n1460\t\n1461\t# === Test 5: Stale reclamation as side effect ===\n1462\t# Dead worker's bead is reclaimed when another worker claims\n1463\tbf claim --any --assignee \"scavenger\" --json\n1464\t# scavenger gets a bead; dead-worker's bead is also reclaimed to open\n1465\t\n1466\t# === Test 6: Multi-workspace claiming ===\n1467\t# Create two workspaces, claim --any gets highest priority across both\n1468\tmkdir /tmp/ws-a && cd /tmp/ws-a && bf init --prefix wa\n1469\tmkdir /tmp/ws-b && cd /tmp/ws-b && bf init --prefix wb\n1470\tbf create --title \"ws-a high\" --priority 0   # in ws-b\n1471\tbf create --title \"ws-a low\"  --priority 4   # in ws-b\n1472\tcd /tmp/ws-a && bf create --title \"ws-a mid\" --priority 2\n1473\tbf claim --any --assignee \"multi-worker\" --json --workspace /tmp/ws-a --workspace /tmp/ws-b\n1474\t# Should get ws-b's \"ws-a high\" (priority 0)\n1475\t```\n1476\t\n1477\t---\n1478\t\n1479\t## Implementation Order\n1480\t\n1481\t| Phase | Description | Estimated Effort |\n1482\t|-------|-------------|-----------------|\n1483\t| 1 | Core library (model, JSONL read/write, config, ID gen) | Foundation |\n1484\t| 2 | SQLite cache layer (schema, storage, sync, doctor) | Medium |\n1485\t| 3 | CLI commands (all br-compatible commands) | Medium |\n1486\t| 4 | Concurrent claiming (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, impact scoring, stale reclamation, multi-workspace) | Medium |\n1487\t| 4B | Extended features (log rotation, batch ops, annotations, operation history, secret scanning, critical path, velocity scoring) | Medium |\n1488\t| 5 | NEEDLE integration (pluck.sh update, backward compat) | Small |\n1489\t| 6 | Build & deploy (CI, binary) | Small |\n1490\t\n1491\tPhases 1-3 produce a fully functional standalone `bf` that replaces `br`. Phase 4 adds atomic claiming for fleet operations. Phase 4B adds extended features that make bf more powerful than br. Phases 5-6 integrate and deploy.\n1492\t\n1493\t---\n1494\t\n1495\t## Key Design Decisions\n1496\t\n1497\t1. **SQLite-primary, JSONL as git artifact**: SQLite is the live database — all reads and writes go through it. JSONL is exported on `bf sync` for git commit, providing backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. This matches how bd and br work, but with rusqlite (no corruption) and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim (no race condition).\n1498\t\n1499\t2. **rusqlite, not FrankenSQLite**: We already proved in the beads_rust fork that FrankenSQLite has corruption issues. Start clean with rusqlite.\n1500\t\n1501\t3. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim**: The read-score-update sequence runs in a single SQLite write transaction. No flock, no streaming rewrite, no temp files. SQLite's own locking serializes concurrent claims correctly.\n1502\t\n1503\t4. **No automatic git commits**: Match br's explicit, non-invasive philosophy. Users run `bf sync` when they want to commit JSONL changes.\n1504\t\n1505\t5. **Cattle, not pets**: Workers are disposable fleet units with no identity, no memory, and no conversation. Claims are atomic SQL dequeues from a priority queue, not negotiations.\n1506\t\n1507\t6. **Stale reclamation as a side effect of claiming**: The first statement in every `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` claim transaction resets expired `in_progress` beads. No separate heartbeat system, no background process.\n1508\t\n1509\t7. **Server as future optimization, not v1**: A persistent in-memory server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms to ~0.1ms by eliminating SQLite file I/O. Premature for current scale — can be added transparently later.\n1510\t\n1511\t8. **Rotation keeps JSONL artifact lean**: Closed beads older than `rotate_age_days` are exported to archive files (`issues.jsonl.1`, etc.) rather than the active `issues.jsonl`. Keeps the committed artifact small and git diffs readable.\n1512\t\n1513\t9. **Annotations as extension mechanism**: Arbitrary `BTreeMap<String, String>` on beads lets external tools (NEEDLE, custom scripts) store structured metadata without schema changes. Stored in a separate `bead_annotations` table — never as a column on `issues` — because br's `issues_column_order_matches()` triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` on any column count mismatch, silently destroying any extra column on every br open. br never reads or writes `bead_annotations`, so annotation data survives any br operation unchanged.\n1514\t\n1515\t10. **Events table for history**: Every mutation records an event row. `bf log` queries the events table — O(1) by issue ID. Long-term history via git log on `issues.jsonl`.\n1516\t\n1517\t11. **Secret scanning before write**: Built-in regex-based secret detection prevents credentials from entering SQLite or the JSONL export. Configurable patterns, git pre-commit hook integration.\n1518\t\n1519\t12. **`.beads/` is committed to git**: `issues.jsonl` + config are version-controlled. `beads.db` is gitignored (binary, rebuilt from JSONL on `bf sync --import`). Secret scanning protects the exported JSONL.\n1520\t\n1521\t13. **Critical path drives claim priority, not just listed priority**: Listed priority is a human signal, but it decays as the project evolves and humans stop curating it. Critical path float is computed from the live dependency graph and is always current. A priority-3 bead on the critical path outranks a priority-0 bead with float=5 — the fleet naturally works on what matters most without human recuration.\n1522\t\n1523\t14. **Worker composition is first-class metadata**: `--model`, `--harness`, `--harness-version` on `bf claim` record what kind of agent did the work. This transforms the events table from a bare audit log into a performance dataset: which model+harness combinations close which task types fastest. The fleet becomes self-optimizing — velocity data informs which workers to dispatch to which workspace, without any external ML pipeline.\n1524\t\n1525\t---\n1526\t\n1527\t## Alternative Approaches Considered\n1528\t\n1529\t### In-Memory Server (deferred)\n1530\t\n1531\tThe plan originally included a coordination server: persistent process, Unix socket protocol, `Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>`, in-memory BTreeMap priority queues, heartbeat-based stale detection. This was deferred to a future optimization because SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` delivers sufficient throughput at current scale.\n1532\t\n1533\tThe server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms (SQLite transaction) to ~0.1ms (memory pop). This matters only if fleets exceed 50 workers or claim frequency exceeds ~500/sec — neither is on the horizon. The server can be added transparently: `bf claim` detects the server socket, delegates if present, falls back to SQLite if not.\n1534\t\n1535\t### MCP Agent Mail (Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust)\n1536\t\n1537\tJeffrey Emanuel's companion system for inter-agent coordination. A Rust MCP server with 36 tools, 33 resources, Git-backed archive, SQLite indexing, HTTP/TUI/Robot surfaces.\n1538\t\n1539\t**Architecture**: Agents register identities, claim file reservations with TTL, exchange threaded messages, negotiate work assignments via acknowledgements. Coordination happens through conversation — \"I'm taking src/auth/**, can you work on tests/?\"\n1540\t\n1541\t**Why it doesn't fit bead-forge**: Agent Mail is built for the **pets** model — named, persistent agents that maintain identity across sessions, negotiate via messaging, and coordinate through conversation. NEEDLE uses the **cattle** model — disposable workers that are interchangeable, stateless, and need atomic dequeue without any conversation.\n1542\t\n1543\t| Aspect | Agent Mail (Pets) | bead-forge (Cattle) |\n1544\t|--------|-------------------|---------------------|\n1545\t| Agent identity | Registered, named, persistent | Anonymous, stateless, disposable |\n1546\t| Work assignment | Negotiation, messaging, agreement | Atomic SQL dequeue (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) |\n1547\t| Coordination mechanism | Threaded messages, acknowledgements | Kernel-provided mutual exclusion |\n1548\t| File/workspace ownership | Advisory file reservations | None — beads are the unit of work |\n1549\t| Communication pattern | Multi-turn conversation | Single CLI invocation |\n1550\t| Failure mode | Agent re-joins conversation | Agent dies, claim TTL expires, bead reopens |\n1551\t| Agent count | Small (3-5 named agents) | Large fleet (11-20+ disposable workers) |\n1552\t\n1553\t**What to borrow from Agent Mail**:\n1554\t- **TTL-based claim expiration**: Agent Mail uses TTL on file reservations. bead-forge applies the same concept — claims older than `claim_ttl` are reclaimed to `open` on the next claim invocation.\n1555\t\n1556\t**What to explicitly reject**:\n1557\t- **Agent identities**: Workers don't register or maintain identity. The `--assignee` field is for logging, not identity.\n1558\t- **Messaging/threading**: Workers don't send messages to each other. The only communication is claim/close through the JSONL file.\n1559\t- **File reservations**: Workers operate on entire beads, not file-level reservations.\n1560\t- **MCP layer**: bead-forge is a CLI. No stdio-based MCP protocol.\n1561\t- **Advisory locks**: Claims are enforced by `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, not advisory. Once claimed (inside the transaction), no other worker sees that bead as open.\n1562\t\n1563\t### BeadHub (juanre/beadhub)\n1564\t\n1565\tA coordination server for AI agent teams built on top of Steve Yegge's Dolt-based `bd`. The `bdh` CLI wraps `bd` and adds work claiming, file reservation, presence awareness, and inter-agent messaging. Includes a web dashboard.\n1566\t\n1567\t**Why it doesn't fit**: Tied to Dolt-based `bd` architecture (not JSONL). bead-forge needs JSONL+SQLite compatibility with br, not Dolt compatibility with bd. However, the coordination server concept validates that this problem is real and worth solving.\n1568\t\n1569\t### Beads Viewer (Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer)\n1570\t\n1571\tGraph-aware TUI with PageRank-based prioritization, critical path analysis, and kanban board view.\n1572\t\n1573\t**Why it doesn't fit**: Read-only visualization tool.
